newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gunmen kidnap high school girls in Algiers -paper.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kidnap high school girls in Algiers -paper.

text.p: Gunmen thought to be Moslem guerrillas have abducted two high school girls on their way to their classes in Algiers, an Algerian newspaper said on Wednesday.
La Tribune newspaper said the girls, aged 16 and 18 years, were abducted on Tuesday in Bouzareah, a Moslem stronghold on the northern edge of the Algerian capital.
Attacks against schools, teachers and students have been a frequent feature of Algeria's five-year-old civil strife locking up the North African country's government and Moslem rebels.
Suspected Moslem guerrillas abducted two high school girls on their way to school two weeks ago in Medea, 70 km (45 miles) southwest of Algiers. Security forces are still searching for them.
More than 500 teachers and students have perished in Moslem guerrilla attacks in the past three years. At least 700 schools were also set ablaze in a rebel sabotage campaign.
